title: Federal and state judicial responsibilities
summary: Federalism distributes judicial and lawmaking responsibilities between the national government and the states. Procedure can affect that distribution through jurisdiction, governing law, and the treatment of state-created rights.
notes: A general appeal to federalism does not replace the specific test. Grable, Hanna, and personal-jurisdiction cases give the concern different legal roles.

sections.Meaning: Federalism distributes judicial and lawmaking responsibilities between the national government and the states. Procedure can affect that distribution through jurisdiction, governing law, and the treatment of state-created rights.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify which institution is acting and the source of its authority. In jurisdiction, consider the category Congress has assigned to federal courts. In Erie problems, identify the disputed state rule and the competing federal source. In personal jurisdiction, consider the constitutional protection applied in the particular state or federal setting.
